# text: a short summary written by Danish Quantum Academy from the profile's own research description (Short presentation,
# Primary fields of research, Current research, Keywords); CV sections are not used. Empty when the profile has no description.

column3: Mathematical physics: Bose and Fermi gases, the stability of atoms and molecules, and thermodynamic stability, using spectral theory, partial differential equations and the calculus of variations.

Studies how quantum mechanics changes information processing, with contributions of an algorithmic, cryptographic and information-theoretic kind. Leads the Quantum for Life Center and the UCPH Quantum Hub, and is co-PI of QMATH.
Works on the mathematical aspects of quantum mechanics; principal investigator of the ERC Advanced Grant MathBEC on Bose–Einstein condensation (2023–28).

Quantum computing theory: for which tasks quantum technologies give an advantage. Central themes are entanglement and nonlocal games, self-testing of quantum devices, algorithms based on Schur–Weyl duality, the commuting versus tensor-product models of entanglement, and the complexity of entanglement-assisted protocols.

Theoretical physics aimed at using quantum technology for applications, above all simulating many-body physics in materials and chemistry with classical and quantum methods. Proposes experiments for neutral atoms and superconducting circuits.

Quantum information and computation: how to characterise and quantify noise in quantum systems and how it limits or helps information processing; also convex optimisation algorithms inspired by quantum mechanics and tensor networks.

Theoretical condensed matter physics: quantum effects in electron transport in devices and in quantum information processing systems, lately topological superconductors, superconductor–semiconductor hybrids and Majorana bound states. Director of the Center for Quantum Devices.
Geometric analysis and partial differential equations in Riemannian, conformal and Kähler geometry, with links to mathematical physics.

Leads QUANTOP – Quantum Optics Center at the Niels Bohr Institute. Works on the quantum physics of matter and light, quantum communication, quantum sensing and quantum information technologies, including teleportation between material objects, quantum memory for light and measurements beyond the Heisenberg uncertainty limit.
